chunks.text: Today we will talk about Namibia.
Namibia is a country with deserts, wild animals, and beautiful landscapes.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Where is Namibia?
Namibia is in southern Africa.
It is next to Angola, Zambia, Botswana, and South Africa.
To the west, it touches the Atlantic Ocean.
Namibia is known for its wide open land and dry deserts.
What is the capital city of Namibia?
The capital city is Windhoek, say Windhoek.
It is in the middle of the country.
Windhoek has shops, markets, offices, and schools.
Other towns include Swachupmund on the coast with German -style buildings, Walvis Bay of Port City, Rundu and Oshakati near the north.
How many people live in Namibia?
About two seven million people live in Namibia.
That is not many.
It is one of the least crowded countries in the world.
Most people live in villages, small towns, or close to water.
What language do people speak in Namibia?
The official language is English, but many people also speak Oshihwambo -Africans, German -Herero, Nama, and other local languages.
People often speak two or three languages every day.
What is the weather like in Namibia?
Namibia has a dry and sunny climate, very hot in summer, October to March, cool at night, even in the desert, little rain mostly in January and February.
The sky is often blue and clear.
What does Namibia look like?
Namibia has the name of desert with red sand dunes, the Kalahari Desert with grass and animals, mountains, plains, and canyons, the skeleton coast with shipwrecks and fog.
Namibia is a land of strong beauty and quiet nature.
What animals live in Namibia?
Namibia has many wild animals such as elephants, lions, and leopards, zebras, giraffes, and rhinos, springbox, oryx, and cheetahs, flamingos, pelicans, and eagles.
People can visit Atosha National Park to see animals in the wild.
What do people eat in Namibia?
Namibian food is simple, local, and meat -based.

People eat meat, like beef, goat, or game, wild meat, tap, maize porridge, eaten with sauce or meat, beans, pumpkin, and greens, fish especially near the coast, popular foods, capana, grilled street meat, vet coke, fried bread filled with meat, bribelice, meat cooked over fire.
Oshafima, a traditional maize meal.
What do people drink in Namibia?
People drink water, tea and coffee, fruit juice.
Adults may drink beer, homemade brews, or soft drinks.
In some places, people also drink Mahungu beer, made from millet.
What is life like in Namibia?
Life in Namibia can be very different in the city and in the village.
In the village, people live in simple homes.
They grow food, keep animals, and cook over a fire.
Life is quiet and natural.
In the city, people go to school, offices, and shops.
There is internet, TV, and modern transport.
Everywhere, family and tradition are important.
What are some holidays and traditions in Namibia?
Independence Day, March 21, Heroes Day, August 26,
Christmas with food and family, Easter with music and prayer, traditional weddings with singing and dancing.
Many people wear colorful clothes and enjoy storytelling and music.
Some fun facts about Namibia.
The name of desert is one of the oldest deserts in the world.
Namibia has more cheetahs than any other country.
The flag has blue, red, green, white, and a gold sun.
German is still spoken in some towns from colonial history.
You can see the stars clearly at night.
The sky is amazing.
Now you know many things about Namibia.
You know where it is, what people eat, and how they live.
You learned about deserts, animals, and traditions.
Well done.
Thank you for listening to the Slow English Podcast.
I am Emily.
See you next time.
Goodbye or in Oshihwambo, Tatili.
